summary.description: Usually white crystalline solids that are generally unreactive with low water solubility and low vapor pressure. They adsorb to soils and sediments, resulting in low atmospheric concentrations
environmental_impact: Toxic to wildlife, particularly aquatic organisms
Act as hormone disrupting substances mimicking animal hormones
Can be transported far from original release point
Pose long-term threat to wildlife populations

top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Octylphenols are particularly toxic to aquatic organisms and bio-accumulate in marine environments. As hormone disrupting substances, they interfere with reproductive systems of fish and other aquatic life, threatening biodiversity and ecosystem health. Their persistence and long-range transport capabilities make them a significant threat to marine ecosystems worldwide.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: These pollutants contaminate water systems through releases from cleaning products and industrial processes. Their persistence in the environment and ability to adsorb to sediments means they can compromise water quality for extended periods, affecting both human water supplies and aquatic ecosystem health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Octylphenols are widely used in consumer products including detergents, rubber, plastics, and cleaning products. Their environmental persistence and hormone-disrupting properties necessitate a shift toward more sustainable production methods and responsible consumption patterns to minimize their release into the environment while maintaining product functionality.
